newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia airlines plan no jet fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia airlines plan no jet fuel surcharge.

text.p: Australian airlines said on Monday that they had no plans to impose any surcharges on cargo rates or passenger fares in light of the rise in the jet fuel price.
Both Qantas Airways Ltd and Ansett Airlines Ltd said they are closely monitoring the movement in the jet fuel price, and their pricing policy may change accordingly.
"We have no plans to put up our fares in response to what it happening elsewhere," Ansett public affairs officer Geoff Lynch told Reuters.
Lynch said this applied to both cargo and passenger services.
"There are no plans to raise fares," Qantas public affairs officer Julian Green said referring to both cargo and passenger services.
Airlines in the Asia Pacific are considering putting up both cargo and passenger fares as long as fuel prices show no sign of coming down.
Some airlines in Europe region have already announced plans to raise prices.
